source_text: Verum iam Apostoli verba videamus, quem mihi ad omnia, quae supra posui, respondere dixisti: Ad omnia ista huic respondit Apostolus, qui neque voluntatem arguit parvuli, quae propria in illo nondum est ad peccandum; neque nuptias, in quantum nuptiae sunt, quae habent a Deo non solum institutionem, verum etiam benedictionem; neque parentes, in quantum parentes sunt, invicem licite atque legitime ad procreandos filios coniugati; sed: " Per unum - inquit - hominem peccatum intravit in mundum, et per peccatum mors; et ita in omnes homines pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt " [n34] . Quod isti si catholicis auribus mentibusque perciperent, adversum fidem gratiamque Christi rebelles animos non haberent, neque conarentur inaniter, ad suum proprium et haereticum sensum haec apostolica verba tam dilucida et tam manifesta convertere, asserentes hoc ideo dictum esse, quod Adam peccaverit primum, in quo de cetero, quisquis peccare voluit, peccandi invenit exemplum; ut peccatum scilicet non generatione ab illo uno in omnes homines, sed illius unius imitatione transire, cum profecto, si Apostolus hic imitationem intellegi voluisset, non per unum hominem, sed per diabolum potius, in hunc mundum peccatum intrasse, et per omnes homines pertransisse dixisset. De diabolo quippe scriptum est: " Imitantur eum, qui sunt ex parte ipsius " [n35] . Sed ideo " per unum hominem " - dixit - a quo generatio utique hominum coepit, ut per generationem doceret isse per omnes originale peccatum [n36] .
pass_a_gloss: But now let us see the Apostle's words, whom you said answers me to all things which I set down above: To all those things the Apostle answers this man, who accuses neither the will of the little child, which as his own is not yet in him toward sinning; nor marriages, insofar as they are marriages, which have from God not only institution but also blessing; nor the parents, insofar as they are parents, joined to one another licitly and legitimately toward procreating children; but: 'Through one,' he says, 'human being sin entered into the world, and through sin death; and so it passed through into all human beings, in whom all sinned.' Which if these people perceived with catholic ears and minds, they would not have souls rebellious against the faith and grace of Christ, nor would they try emptily to turn these apostolic words, so lucid and so manifest, to their own proper and heretical sense, asserting that this was said for this reason, that Adam sinned first, in whom for the rest whoever wished to sin found an example of sinning; so that, namely, sin would pass not by generation from that one into all human beings, but by imitation of that one, when surely, if the Apostle had wanted imitation to be understood here, he would have said that sin entered into this world not through one human being but rather through the devil, and passed through all human beings. For of the devil it is written: 'They imitate him, who are from his party.' But for this reason he said 'through one human being,' from whom the generation of human beings certainly began, that he might teach that original sin went through all by generation.

pass_b_english: But let us now examine the words of the apostle, whom you said answers everything I set out above. You write: ‘The apostle answers all these points for him. He accuses neither the infant’s will, which does not yet exist in the infant as a personal will capable of sin; nor marriage, insofar as it is marriage, which has not only its institution but also its blessing from God; nor the parents, insofar as they are parents, lawfully and legitimately joined to one another to produce children. Instead he says: “Through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin; and so it passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned” (Romans 5:12). If these people received this with catholic ears and minds, they would not have hearts rebelling against Christ’s faith and grace. Nor would they vainly try to twist these completely clear and evident apostolic words into their own peculiar, heretical meaning. They claim that this was said because Adam sinned first, and thereafter anyone who wished to sin found in him an example of sinning. Thus, they say, sin passed from that one man into all human beings, not by generation but by imitation of that one man. Yet surely, if the apostle had meant imitation here, he would have said that sin entered this world and passed through all human beings through the devil, rather than through one man. For Scripture says of the devil: “Those who belong to his party imitate him” (Wisdom 2:24; Latin numbering 2:25). But he said “through one man,” from whom the generation of human beings certainly began, precisely to teach that original sin passed through all people by generation’ (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.45).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: The Latin text of Romans 5:12 says in quo, rendered here as “in whom”; the interpretation of these words is part of the dispute. Wisdom’s wording and verse division follow the Latin quotation; modern Wisdom 2:24 corresponds to Latin 2:24–25.
